parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High Risk: no general ban on trans identity or execution, but the visitor faces two universal exposures—national border/document screening that can refuse entry or support a lifetime fraud finding when sex markers are doubted, and a division facilities law (effective 1 July 2025) excluding trans people from birth-sex multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters in public facilities. State public-accommodation and hate-crime protections are absent; national hate-crime and employment law do not remedy these visitor-facing rules. Detention/custody carries documented severe harm. Minors face school-facility and youth-care restrictions. Existing X passports and non-automatic fraud findings are limited mitigants; litigation is unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules bar new X markers, require sex assigned at birth, and border cable tells officers to refuse cases with sex discrepancy or reasonable doubt; possible material-misrepresentation/lifetime ineligibility finding; reports of confiscated or blocked passports.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is not automatic; litigation challenges the policy.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign visitor with X or mismatched marker may be refused entry or visa, questioned, or referred; the home passport cannot be altered locally.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections conversion practices include hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no documented visitor-specific custody safeguard or consular remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can lead to immigration detention; custody placement and care then follow national practices, not division protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law effective 1 July 2025 requires public multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex; schools pre-K-12 birth-sex restrooms; civil cause of action; no state public-accommodation protection.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statutory exemptions for assistance, emergency and maintenance; reasonable accommodation for students unwilling to use birth-sex multiple-occupancy facilities; three city ordinances.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using public facilities or travelling with a minor may be excluded, ejected or face a civil complaint; accommodations do not permit opposite-sex multi-occupancy access.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors and restricts trans sports; no state nondiscrimination in care; national proposals target insurance for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: No visitor-specific care protection is documented; national employment discrimination protection is not care access.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor routine or emergency care exposure is not documented; a trans minor travelling with a guardian faces the state youth-care ban if care is sought.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; justice reward memo references 'radical gender ideology'; executive order directs prosecuting teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; counterterrorism document says powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises official hostility and reporting or outing risk; teacher-prosecution order reaches schools and minors, not ordinary adult visitor conduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school restroom law applies pre-K-12; youth gender-affirming care is banned; national executive order threatens teachers using preferred names or pronouns; facilities law covers sleeping and changing areas.
minors_guardians.protection: Reasonable accommodation for students not wishing birth-sex multiple-occupancy facilities; statutory exemptions; national litigation.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor visiting or using public facilities may be directed to birth-sex facilities; a guardian may face friction; access to care is restricted.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime statute; no state public-accommodation, housing or employment gender-identity protection; only national hate-crime statute and three city ordinances. No state-specific incident count is sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment discrimination protection; local ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence would rely on national hate-crime authority; state gaps leave thin local recourse, but prevalence is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No working state public-accommodation remedy; facility-law challenge and enforcement unknown; passport litigation unresolved; possible lifetime fraud finding.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts and litigation; fraud finding not automatic; existing X passports valid; national hate-crime and employment protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Visitor remedies depend on national litigation and border discretion; state law offers no accommodation recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar border-refusal/no-detention scenario, but this dossier adds a statewide public-facilities exclusion, possible lifetime fraud finding and documented custody harm, so it rates lower (more risk) than this anchor.
Anchor has an ombudsman securing release and no detention; here no working visitor remedy is documented for facilities or border refusal, and custody harm is documented, so lower.

Anchor has a functioning charter protecting a trans traveller despite friction; this regime has universal exclusion and unresolved border sanctions, with no comparable operative protection, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system combines national border/document screening that can refuse entry or trigger a lifetime fraud finding with a division public-facilities law excluding trans people from birth-sex multi-occupancy spaces. National hate-crime and employment protections are real but do not remedy those visitor-facing exposures. Custody and immigration detention carry documented severe harm, and minors face school-facility and care restrictions. Existing X passports, non-automatic fraud findings and pending litigation are limited mitigants, not working visitor remedies.
